messages:
raj: heads up — after the kernel selector landing yesterday I'm seeing a reproducible tail regression on mixtral-moe. 95p generation latency up ~2.5x when router top_k >= 48.
ciara: ugh, did we change any router logits normalization or the softmax temperature in the rollout? :eyes:
raj: no explicit router code changes aside from kernel mapping for attention matmul -> cutlass variant. suspect kernel path changed perf characteristics under high expert contention + kv cache thrash.
alex: can you paste a short perf trace and an example config?
raj: reproducer: small batch (B=4), seq=1024, mixtral-moe-32e, top_k=64, routing=probabilistic. command: `./run_serv_bench --model mixtral-moe --batch 4 --seq 1024 --topk 64 --routes probabilistic --profile nvtx`
raj: nvprof output (trimmed):
```
GPU time (ms)  | kernel
--------------|---------------------------
0.34          | cutlass_gemm_fp16
2.87          | router_logits_softmax
5.12          | kv_cache_lookup
9.48          | expert_forward_kernel_cutlass
```

raj: previously expert_forward_kernel was ~4.0 ms; now 9.4 under same load. kv_cache_lookup also doubled.
maria: kv cache doubling looks like upstream eviction churn. Any change to prefix caching or kv shard layout?
raj: we flipped to the new prefix-KV eviction heuristic (LRU-ish) in the canary. suspect it's causing hotset thrash with top-k routing because many requests land on same small set of experts and evict others.
loren: that aligns — topk=64 increases expert overlap which pushes cache working set size. The new kernel mapping also increased per-expert kernel latency (cutlass tiling mismatch for head/kv dims).
ciara: two vectors then: (1) routing-induced working set growth, (2) kernel selection suboptimal for current kv/head dims. we should triage both.
alex: quick experiment idea: force old kernel path on canary for expert_forward and run same reproducer; and second experiment: cap top_k to 32 and measure tail.
raj: I ran both: forcing old kernel restores expert_forward to 4.1ms and P95 goes back to normal. capping top_k to 32 reduces kv_cache_lookup time by ~45%.
bench-bot: benchmark summary uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/mixtral/moe/topk-kernel-regress/3221112223/report.html
ciara: good — kernel switch is the proximate cause. can infra snapshot the cutlass config differences? @infra-bot can you dump the mapping?
infra-bot: dumping kernel mapping for cluster canary-3... done. file: /var/log/kernel-maps/canary-3-3221112223.json
loren: looking through mapping — cutlass tile changed from 128x128 -> 256x64 for the expert gemm path due to heuristic that favored memory throughput for long sequences. that tile performs badly for kv dims where head_dim is 64/128; it increases register pressure and stalls.
maria: proposed fixes: 1) revert kernel mapping for expert_forward for moe models until we implement a head_dim-aware selector, 2) add softbalance routing throttle that reduces effective top_k when kv cache miss rate > X, 3) add telemetry (per-expert kv hit/miss + kernel choice) to Console.
raj: agree. small rollout plan: revert mapping on canary immediately, add experiment to adaptive-topk (softbalance) where router reduces top_k by 25% when cache miss > 12% for same req stream. canary window 30m.
ciara: add an A/B variant that keeps new mapping but uses a kernel fallback path when a single expert's latency > 8ms for 3 consecutive requests. that will let us gather perf counters without full revert.
alex: note: need to validate that fallback doesn't blow up memory or increase GPU context switches. include nvprof counters for SM_occupancy and regs-per-thread in the telemetry.
raj: I'll open a short runbook and start the canary revert now. putting quick notes in the thread: what to watch: P95 gen latency, per-expert kv miss rate, expert_forward kernel ms, GPU SM occupancy.
loren: also watch for increased network fanout if softbalance reduces top_k — could up bandwidth and routing pressure.
maria: i'll prepare console dashboard widgets for kv miss rate and per-kernel latency. tagging eng-sre for alert thresholds.
alex: thanks — one more thought: RoPE scaling changes can alter rope head dim alignment and shift kernel perf characteristics for cutlass. if we change RoPE scaling in future, add a perf test matrix for head_dim x tile_size.
raj: noted. i'll file follow-up to add matrix. thanks all :thumbsup:
